This answers it directly — concise summary:

**Login** — `AuthService.login()` (`frontend/src/app/services/auth.service.ts:16`) is name-only: it loads `localStorage["ai_dnd_user_<lowercase name>"]` or creates an empty `UserProfile`, stores it under `ai_dnd_user`, and sets the `profile` signal. No server call, no password. `isLoggedIn()` (`:12`) is just `profile() !== null`, enforced by `auth.guard.md`.

**Campaigns storage** — Campaign slots (`CampaignSlot`) live only in the browser, inside each `UserProfile` under `localStorage` keys `ai_dnd_user` (active) and `ai_dnd_user_<name>` (per-user). A slot just points at a Worker `sessionId` + `characterId`; the actual game data (character, inventory, log) is server-side in D1, and live session state (location, combat, last 20 history turns) is in Workers KV under `session:<sessionId>` with a 7-day TTL.

**Deleting a campaign slot** — `AuthService.removeCampaign()` (`auth.service.ts:54`) **only deletes the local slot/link**. It never calls the Worker. So the server-side character in D1 (`characters`, `character_inventory`, `adventure_log`) and the KV session are untouched — they remain in the database, just orphaned (nothing in the browser points to them anymore).
